outline: Modern control theory mainly focuses on linear system analysis and design.  This is the course where students from a variety of backgrounds begin to acquire the mathematical tools used in research literature involving linear systems.  The core material covered in this course is the theory of time-varying linear systems, in both continuous-time and discrete-time, with frequent specialization to the time invariant case.
schedule:
Tentative schedule

2	Background linear algebra
3	Mathematical descriptions of systems
4	Linearization
5	State-space solutions
6	System realizations

8	Lyapunov theorem
9 	Stability of LTV systems
10	Controllability
11	Observability
12	Midterm exam
13	Coprime fractions
14	Minimal realizations
15	State feedback
16	Paper presentations I
17	Paper presentations II or optional Final exam
18	Reports for presentations due

PS: The contents and order of lectures and presentations will be adjusted according to actual needs
assessment: The final grade will be a weighted average of attendance 10%, homework (including quizzes) 30%, midterm 30%, paper presentation and report  (and/or optional final examination) 30%.
